title: Counter loop rounds
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$ and $S$ be types with decidable equality, let $x$ be a finite input word over $\Gamma$, let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape machine over $\Gamma$ with states in $S$. Fix a state $a\in S$, an optional exit state, a time function $\tau$ on configurations, an initial configuration $c$, a Boolean word $w$, a tape $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$, a position $cp\in\mathbb Z$, and a natural number $n$; suppose that for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, the tape cell $ct(cp+p)$ contains the symbol stored at offset $p$ in the word $w$ with its bits mapped by $e$ (and is blank when that offset is outside the word), and that $n$ is at most the natural number represented by the binary digits of $w$. Suppose also that, for every $r<n$, the configuration after $r$ counter-loop rounds has state $a$, its prescribed duration is positive, and at each strictly intermediate positive time the machine is in a state different from $a$ and different from the designated exit state. Then after the sum of those $n$ durations plus the counter overhead, the counter-loop machine started with counter state in its initial decrement phase is in the configuration obtained from the $n$-round orbit of $c$ by redirecting its state (with the initial decrement phase used when $n=0$), and by replacing the counter segment of $ct$ with the word obtained after $n$ fixed-width decrements, mapped by $e$. Throughout this run, before the final time the machine has not reached either exit anchor; at every time up to and including the final time, the counter head remains between $cp-1$ and $cp+|w|$, inclusive, and the other work-head positions satisfy the stated round-by-round condition: at each such time they equal those of the base machine at some time within one of the first $n$ rounds, or at time zero of round $n$.

the exit is an optional state in $S$

for every $r<n$, the round-orbit configuration has state $a$
for every $r<n$, its duration is positive
at every strictly intermediate positive time in each such round, the state is neither $a$ nor the designated exit state
